Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Clonal recurrence test with split-population barcoding ("recur")
ideas.description: Transduce the cell line with a high-complexity heritable barcode library (e.g., ClonMapper/Watermelon), split the labeled population into replicate arms, treat each independently, and sequence barcodes in the survivors. The degree of barcode overlap between arms quantifies how much survival is driven by a heritable, pre-existing clonal state versus a stochastic, non-heritable coin flip, and a barcode-plus-scRNA readout links each recurring clone to its expression program.

ideas.title: Retrospective unmasking of the pre-treatment survivor state ("unmask")
ideas.description: Use a Rewind-style approach: image and single-cell-profile the untreated population, then apply drug, identify the rare survivors, and trace them back to their fixed/imaged ancestors (via live-cell tracking or barcode-guided recovery of the initial-state scRNA-seq profiles). This directly measures what the surviving cells looked like before drug exposure, rather than inferring cause from the post-treatment state, which is confounded by drug-induced reprogramming.

ideas.title: Sister-cell divergence to measure the memory timescale ("twinter")
ideas.description: Live-image a reporter for a candidate priming factor (e.g., AXL, NGFR, or an ERK/EGFR activity biosensor) across tracked lineages, then treat and score which cells survive, comparing concordance of survival between sister cells, cousins, and unrelated cells as a function of time since division. The decay of concordance with lineage distance gives a quantitative half-life for the fluctuating state that confers tolerance, distinguishing short-lived signaling noise from multi-generation epigenetic memory.

ideas.title: Single-cell metabolic phenotyping of the quiescent/starved state ("semifamine")
ideas.description: Apply label-free NAD(P)H/FAD fluorescence lifetime imaging plus SCENITH or puromycin-incorporation assays to measure per-cell translation rate, glycolytic/oxidative balance, and cell-cycle position at the moment of drug addition, then follow the same cells to survival outcome. This tests whether survivors occupy a dormant, low-biosynthesis, lipid-peroxidation-sensitive niche, and nominates metabolic co-treatments (e.g., GPX4 or OXPHOS inhibition) whose efficacy should track the measured state.

ideas.title: Spatial accounting of dying neighbors and local niche effects ("ghostcraft")
ideas.description: Perform longitudinal imaging of the whole treated monolayer or 3D culture so that each survivor's local history is recorded: distance to dying cells, local density, time-integrated exposure to apoptotic-corpse-derived and secreted factors, measured against conditioned-media and spatially randomized controls. Pairing this with spatial transcriptomics of survivor neighborhoods distinguishes cell-intrinsic priming from non-cell-autonomous rescue by dying or stressed neighbors, which is testable by blocking candidate ligands.
